title: Task preservation and deferred-loading: console routing notes
summary: Working notes for how the console should preserve in-progress work across navigation, use deferred loading to reduce initial payload, and expose shareable 'task snapshots' as deep links. Includes wireframe text sketches, UX tradeoffs, and a groomed backlog with acceptance criteria.
body:
Context:
We keep hearing two recurring problems in research and support: 1) users lose in-progress config/edits when they navigate around the console (eg. switching from Model detail -> Logs -> back), and 2) the console initial load is heavy for teams with many projects/routes. This doc explores a combined approach: preserve user task state in memory and compact URL snapshots + use deferred component loading and background hydration to reduce perceived latency.
body_continued:
Goals (what success looks like):
- No accidental loss: when a user leaves a page with unsaved changes, we persist the working draft automatically (local+server sync) and restore on return.
- Fast perceived navigation: first-paint and route-change should feel snappy; large panes (profiling, traces) should be deferred and hydrated in the background.
- Linkability: every saved or auto-snapshotted task should be shareable via URL with a short snapshot token.
- Predictable memory/cost: limit per-session retained snapshots to N (configurable), evict LRU, and optionally persist to user storage for cross-device restore.
personas: Primary: Platform engineer debugging throughput across models; Secondary: Product manager configuring a rollout. Both need to switch contexts rapidly without losing in-progress edits or losing traceability of steps.
constraints_and_assumptions:
- Console is a single-page app using client-side routes.
- We have a small fast key/value store (indexedDB) available in the browser and a short-lived server-side snapshot store (tokenized).
- Auth is required; snapshot links should be permission-checked server-side.
- Mobile screen constraints will require a compact UI variant (deferred panels collapse).
proposed_flow_and_wireframes:
Sketch A: 'Soft switch' route behavior (text wireframe):
1) User on /projects/alpha/models/ggml-7b/edit with unsaved changes.
2) User clicks 'Logs' -> route transitions to /projects/alpha/models/ggml-7b/logs; top nav shows 'Draft saved (auto) • Restore' for 10s.
3) Large Logs panel deferred: placeholder skeleton + immediate lightweight header + background fetch.
4) If user hits back, we hydrate the draft immediately (no reload) and scroll position restored.

ASCII wireframe (header + two-column):
[Header: project / model / name | breadcrumb token]
[Left column: nav (compact)] [Right column: main pane]
Main pane initial: header + lightweight metrics (fast)
Deferred block: workload profiler (hydrate after 300ms)

URL examples and snapshot tokens:
- Active edit with local snapshot: /p/alpha/m/ggml-7b/edit?draft=local-20241108-9a2
- Shareable server snapshot: /snap/ts-78f4 (server maps token -> compressed state, expires 7d)
- Route with view-only snapshot (for audits): /p/alpha/m/ggml-7b?preview=snap-ts-78f4&mode=view

Routing implications:
- Each route must define a 'snapshot contract' (which pieces of state are required to reconstruct). Lightweight: [form values, scroll pos, active tab, selected node]. Heavy: [profiling cache, timeline indices] should not be included by default.
- Navigation must support 'soft-switch' (switch route while preserving active React tree where possible) vs full remount. Soft-switch reduces re-bootstrap cost but increases memory pressure. We need a heuristic: soft-switch for sibling routes with same top-level schema (e.g., edit <-> settings <-> metrics for a model).

Edge cases and user expectations:
- Unsaved sensitive fields (API keys) must never be persisted without explicit opt-in. Show explicit banner when draft contains secrets.
- If server-side snapshot expires or user loses permission, provide clear fallback: 'Draft available locally only' + export option.
- Multiple tabs: prefer last-active tab for restoring session; show conflict toast when a remote snapshot overwrote local changes.
proposed_backlog_and_estimates:
(Groomed items, rough J-train relative sizes)
1) Route snapshot contract infra — owner: eng-routing — scope: schema + small serializer (3). AC: routes can register keys, sample size < 1KB per snapshot.
2) Local draft store (indexedDB) + autosave (2). AC: autosave every 5s or on route blur; restore on return.
3) Server snapshot token service (4). AC: token create/read/delete, TTL 7d, permission checks.
4) Deferred pane SDK + placeholder primitives (3). AC: consumer can mark component as deferred with threshold, skeleton shown immediately.
5) Soft-switch router behavior (5). AC: sibling routes reuse mounted subtree; memory caps enforced.
6) UI for draft banners + restore flow (1). AC: CTA to restore and explicit 'discard' button.
7) Secret-field redaction rules (2). AC: secret inputs flagged, not included in server snapshots unless user confirms.
8) Shareable link UX + copy flow + analytics (2).
Dependencies: 1 -> required, 2 independent but lower risk, 5 depends on 1 and 4.
Priority: start with 2 and 4 to reduce user pain and perceived latency, then 1 and 5, then server snapshots and UX polish.
acceptance_criteria_examples:
- Autosave: Creating a draft on model edit -> navigate away -> reopen -> draft restored within 500ms on client.
- Deferred: Opening Logs pane should show header/quick stats <150ms and full logs hydrate within 1s on a normal connection.
- Snapshot token: Create token -> open in incognito with same user -> snapshot loads (permission respected) or shows 'no access' if not permitted.
- Secret handling: Draft containing api_key field warns user and excludes that field from server snapshot by default.
open_questions_and_risks:
- How many snapshots per user/session is acceptable? Default 5 or 10? Memory vs UX tradeoff.
- Storage encryption for server snapshots — do we need KV-level encryption now or later? Likely later but flagged for security review.
- Analytics: what events do we log for auto-restore and snapshot create (privacy concerns)?
- QA matrix: cross-browser/edge cases for indexedDB restoration — need test plan.
- Rollback plan: if soft-switch causes memory leaks, we need an abort flag to fall back to full remounts.
next_steps_and_owners:
- Proto spike: implement local draft store + deferred placeholder in a feature branch (owner: Marcus Chen) — due: 2024-12-15.
- Security sync: secret redaction rules + server snapshot encryption decision (owner: Aditi Rao) — due: 2024-12-01.
- Design polish: micro-interaction for snapshot banner and copy link flow (owner: Design) — due: 2024-12-05.
- Grooming session: prioritize items 2,4,1 in next sprint planning (owners: PM + Eng) — schedule: 2024-11-12.
notes_to_reviewers:
Please read the propagation and eviction model in the proposed backlog before sprint planning. Focus feedback on: snapshot contract minimal keys, and whether 'soft-switch' should be opt-in per route or global heuristic. If you have examples of other apps that do this well, paste links in the thread.

Quick links for context: Linear CORE-789, ticket PR-412, and the console routing confluence page (linked above).
editor_notes: Draft — long-form. Intend to split into two smaller PRDs once spike shows feasibility: 1) Client-only autosave & restore, 2) Snapshot token service + UX. Kept lots of implementation detail to help grooming and estimates.
